chapter: Los Angeles with Mutt Carey and the taxi dances
title: Taxi dance halls: Liberty and the One-Eleven
summary: Joe describes the downtown taxi-dance halls, with Tudie's band at One-Eleven, and how dime tickets split with the dancing girls.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Dance halls, lake resorts and where bands played

blocks.x: It was on East Third Street in downtown Los Angeles, the Liberty Dance Hall. And at 111 West Third Street, right across Main Street... That was the dividing line between east and west.
At this time, didn't Tudie have that band at One-Eleven?
At One-Eleven. Tudie had a band upstairs at One-Eleven with the two Walsh boys in it, Ellis Walsh and Everett Walsh. They was from New Orleans.
That was a taxi dance hall, too?
Yes, it was a taxi-dancer. In those days, a taxi dance was a big thing.
Why did they call it "taxi-dance?" I mean, why a taxi?
Well, I don't know exactly where they got the name of taxi. But it was something where the music never stopped...
Maybe because you picked up a partner and dropped them like a taxi picked you up and dropped you?

You made money by the girls dancing. The girls got half. Tickets cost a dime. Say, for instance, if a guy came in and bought ten tickets, the girls would make 50 cents. It was double tickets, and they had a box where the girls had to dance around and deposit one of those tickets in it, and they had a guy standing up by that box watching to see that they threw a ticket in there.
